Hi Laura / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we’re keen to move to an order but need to resolve a couple of legal points before Procurement signs the order form. We’ve attached our proposed redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (Acme_MSA_redline.pdf, OrderForm_SOW_v3.pdf). Two specific asks from Acme Legal:

1) Regulatory fines / statutory penalties (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, PCI) should be carved out from Redwood’s limitation of liability (i.e., excluded from the overall cap).
2) Third-party claims tied to regulatory investigations (e.g., regulator fines, administrative penalties, private actions arising from data incidents) should not be subject to the cap and should sit alongside the indemnities (we included proposed indemnity language).

Our timeline is tight — procurement would like confirmation on whether Redwood can agree in principle within 48 hours to avoid delaying the PO. If you can’t accept all language, please provide alternative wording and any proposed monetary subcaps you’d offer for fines.

Appreciate a quick turnaround.

Best,

Rishi — forwarding Acme’s redlines. They want regulatory fines entirely outside the LoL and third-party claims excluded as well. Ben flagged this as a deal-kicker for them.

Quick notes / asks from me:
- We should avoid an unlimited carve-out for statutory fines. That would be a bad precedent across enterprise deals.
- Propose a negotiation stance: offer a limited carve-out for regulatory fines tied to Vendor’s gross negligence/willful misconduct, with a defined subcap per event and aggregate cap (e.g., $1.5M per event, $3M aggregate), OR exclude only direct statutory fines up to a fixed threshold if Acme insists.
- For third-party claims: prefer to keep these within the overall cap but accept specific indemnities (e.g., IP indemnity) outside the cap. For privacy-related third-party claims, we should be careful — could offer indemnity plus reasonable cooperation.

Can you draft proposed redline language and a fallback position we can present to Acme (Ben needs a 48h reply to Procurement)?

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Liability cap / regulatory fines carve-out (MSA & Order Form)

Laura / Ben — draft language and rationale below. See attached snippet (Liability_Redline_snippet.docx) with explicit replacements. High level: we should avoid broad unlimited exclusions; instead we give a narrowly tailored carve-out that balances Acme’s procurement requirements with our enterprise risk posture.

Proposed MSA clause (redline-ready):
"""
Limitation of Liability. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the parties’ aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) $5,000,000 and (b) twelve (12) months of Fees paid by Customer to Vendor under the applicable Order Form.

Regulatory Fines; Statutory Penalties. Notwithstanding the foregoing limitation of liability, Vendor’s liability for regulatory fines and statutory penalties imposed by a governmental or regulatory authority in connection with Vendor’s material breach of its data protection or security obligations shall be limited as follows: (i) Vendor shall be liable for statutory fines and penalties up to $1,500,000 per incident and $3,000,000 in the aggregate; and (ii) Vendor shall not be liable for fines or penalties to the extent they arise from Customer’s actions or failures, Customer-provided data that violates applicable law, or Customer’s failure to follow Vendor’s documented instructions.

Third-Party Claims. Third-party claims shall be subject to the indemnification and limits set forth in Section [Indemnity]. Notwithstanding the limitation of liability above, Vendor shall indemnify and hold Customer harmless for third-party claims to the extent such claims arise from Vendor’s gross negligence or willful misconduct in connection with data security or privacy.
"""

Negotiation plan / fallback: 
- Primary position: Keep regulatory fines within a defined subcap as above (1.5M per incident / 3M aggregate), tie carve-out to Vendor’s proven breach/gross negligence.
- If Acme insists on full exclusion: propose an alternative where statutory fines are excluded from the LoL but limited to amounts recoverable from Vendor’s commercial general liability and cyber policies (i.e., only to the extent covered by insurance) — we would require confirmation of policy limits.
- For third-party claims: maintain indemnities for IP and willful misconduct outside the cap; privacy-related third-party claims to be indemnified only if caused by Vendor’s gross negligence/willful misconduct.

Risks: Acme may push for an unlimited carve-out citing data sensitivity. If they escalate, Ben may need to trade off price/commitment (e.g., higher cap, enhanced SOC/cert artifacts, or contractual refunds).

Let me know and I’ll prepare a clean redline to send back.

— Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Liability cap / regulatory fines carve-out (MSA & Order Form)

Emily — thanks for the quick note and the redlines. We appreciate Acme’s focus on this. We can move quickly on this and are prepared to offer a compromise to resolve procurement’s concern without creating an open-ended exposure for Redwood.

In short, Redwood’s proposed position is: 
- We will accept a limited carve-out for regulatory fines and statutory penalties that are the direct result of Vendor’s material breach of its security or data protection obligations, capped at $1,500,000 per incident and $3,000,000 aggregate across the term of the Agreement.
- Regulatory fines that arise from Customer’s actions, Customer-provided data, or Customer’s failure to follow Vendor’s documented configuration/integration guidance remain excluded from any vendor liability.
- Third-party claims (private suits) tied to data incidents will generally remain subject to the overall limitation of liability, except that Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims where those claims arise from Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

If Acme needs a different commercial construct (e.g., full exclusion from the cap), we can consider that only if Acme agrees to one of the following: (i) a materially higher aggregate cap (we’d propose $10M), or (ii) an enhanced insurance covenant (proof of cyber liability cover with minimum limits and notice to Redwood of changes).

Please confirm whether Acme can accept the $1.5M/$3M subcap approach or whether Procurement will require us to pursue the insurance/£10M trade-off. If you’re good with the subcap, Rishi will send the exact redline wording and we can lock the order form.

Looking forward — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
